title: Reconstruction Accounts Receivable Terms Schedule: Overdue Draws, Stop-Work, Remobilization, Punch List and Final Payment
content:
The accounts receivable desk applies the following figures to Reconstruction contracts, one row per agreement. All day counts are calendar days.

| Agreement | Grace after a draw's due date | Overdue draw charge per monthly fee period | Stop-work days past due | Remobilization fee | Punch list days | Final payment due days |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Repair Agreement - Minor Repairs | 5 | 1.5% | 7 | $150.00 | 5 | 10 |
| Standard Rebuild Agreement | 5 | 1.5% | 14 | $325.00 | 10 | 15 |
| Major Rebuild Agreement | 5 | 1.5% | 14 | $475.00 | 14 | 15 |
| Full Structural Rebuild Agreement | 5 | 1.5% | 14 | $650.00 | 21 | 15 |
| Multifamily Unit Rebuild Agreement | 10 | 1.5% | 21 | $325.00 | 10 | 30 |
| Commercial Interior Rebuild Agreement | 10 | 1% | 30 | $850.00 | 21 | 30 |

## What each column measures

- **Grace after a draw's due date**: calendar days after a draw's due date before an overdue draw charge may post.
- **Overdue draw charge per monthly fee period**: the charge on an overdue self-paid draw balance for each monthly fee period, as a percentage.
- **Stop-work days past due**: calendar days a draw may be past due before work is suspended.
- **Remobilization fee**: the fee to remobilize the crew after work was suspended for a past-due draw, per suspension, in US dollars.
- **Punch list days**: calendar days after the final walkthrough to complete punch list items.
- **Final payment due days**: calendar days after the final invoice by which the final balance is due.

## Reading across the agreements

The Multifamily Unit Rebuild Agreement and the Commercial Interior Rebuild Agreement carry the longer grace of 10 days; every other agreement carries 5. The Commercial Interior Rebuild Agreement is the only agreement whose monthly overdue percentage is 1% rather than 1.5%. Hypothetical illustration: an agreement with a 1.5% monthly percentage applied to an assumed balance of $2,400.00 gives $36.00 for one fee period.
